- Cross-Departmental Management: Own critical tolerance analysis workflows and drive the resolution of complex interface trade-offs to ensure manufacturability and serviceability

- Mentorship: Act as an internal subject matter expert, coaching engineering teams on GD&T best practices

What you'll bring:

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field; Bachelor's with 8+ years of industry experience in mechanical design, GD&T, interface control, and dimensional management

- Proven ability to build, manage, and scale engineering standards processes within a production-environment

- Exceptional communication skills with the ability to manage standards across diverse, cross-functional teams (Design, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain)

- Experience working with a production manufacturing team and solving problems through dimensional management

Role Description
Form Energy is hiring a Senior Test Engineer to join our Test Engineering team. In this position, you will design, develop, and implement test strategies and prioritizing tests, in partnership with design teams, to ensure the reliability, safety, and performance of our energy storage products. You will leverage your strong background in mechanical and electrical component-level and system-level functional testing skills in order to succeed in this position. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Develop, execute, and own comprehensive test strategies for component, subsystem and system-level testing, including electrical and mechanical performance, characterization, and stress testing, for energy storage system products and their respective components and subsystems.

- Design complex electromechanical test systems and high-voltage architectures.

- Troubleshoot electrical issues in a range of test stands for a variety of purposes.

- Finds and resolves systematic test architecture deficiencies and inefficiencies.

- Leverages hands-on experience and actual technical outcomes to advise on and implement the selection of data acquisition systems and test sensors.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop test cases and procedures covering a range of operating conditions and use cases.

- Analyze large test datasets to identify trends, anomalies, and areas for improvement in product performance and reliability. Correlate test data to theoretical models and simulations as-needed.

- Prepare and deliver detailed test reports summarizing findings, conclusions, and recommendations for design enhancements or corrective actions.

- Drive continuous improvement initiatives to optimize testing processes, increase efficiency, and enhance the overall quality of energy storage products.

What you'll bring:

- Subject Matter Expertise : Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with 4 years of deep technical experience in Test Engineering, data analysis, and a proven track record of leading complex hardware verification programs.

- Data-Driven Strategy : Extensive experience designing and leading test strategies, processing high-bandwidth vibration data, and translating raw results into actionable engineering insights that directly impact product reliability.

- Design Partnership : A demonstrated ability to serve as a strategic partner to Design Engineering, bridging the gap between theoretical design and physical validation to influence early-stage hardware concepts.

- Analytical Rigor : Proficiency in closing the loop between test and analysis, ensuring that empirical data is used to increase the fidelity of static and dynamic models. Sense of urgency and self-driven to hit difficult schedule targets.

- Leadership & Mentorship : A strong desire and demonstrated ability to mentor junior technical staff and coordinate milestone-driven project sub-tasks.

- External Test Lab Partnership : Proficiency in understanding in-house and external lab capabilities, and direct/coordinate test execution at external labs per business needs.

The Mechanical Engineering team at Form designs the battery cell, module, and system enclosure at the core of our utility-scale, multi-day energy storage system — optimized for performance, quality, reliability, and cost at high-volume manufacturing scale at Form Factory.
We're hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to lead our newly formed Modeling, Simulation & Analysis team within the Electro-Mechanical Hardware organization — Form's center of excellence for structural and thermal/fluid simulation (FEA/CFD), mechanical architecture trade studies, and model validation. Your team's analyses will drive design direction before hardware is built, and correlate models against prototype and factory test data so we trust what the models tell us. You'll partner closely with EE, cell performance, system modeling, and reliability engineering, supporting design and build activities on prototype builds in Berkeley, CA and production lines in Weirton, WV.
This is a leadership role: you'll build and mentor the team while staying hands-on in models and reviews. The role reports to the Senior Director of Hardware and Systems Engineering, and will be based at our Berkeley, CA office.

What you'll do:

- Build, manage, and mentor a team of thermal/fluids and structural analysis engineers as a player-coach

- Own structural, thermal, and fluid simulation (FEA/CFD) of Form's iron-air battery cell, module, and enclosure — from early architecture trade studies through production support

- Establish Form's model validation and correlation practice, tying simulation to prototype and factory test data

- Translate product requirements into analysis plans; use simulation results to drive design decisions early in the development cycle

- Collaborate with battery, electrical, chemical, systems, and reliability engineers to optimize designs for performance, cost, and reliability

What you'll bring:

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field with 12+ years of experience (advanced degrees count toward experience — many simulation leaders hold a PhD)

- Deep expertise in either thermal/fluids simulation (CFD/conjugate heat transfer) or structural analysis (FEA, static/dynamic) — with working fluency across both

- Hands-on mastery of commercial CAE tools (e.g., STAR-CCM+, Ansys Fluent/Mechanical/Icepak, Abaqus, COMSOL) and experience automating simulation workflows

- 5+ years of experience managing, building, and leading simulation/analysis (CAE) teams; and mentoring engineers

- Demonstrated model validation/correlation against physical test data

- Strong technical communication across functions and with external partners

Preferred Qualifications

- Mechanical design ownership of shipped hardware products, or experience in high-volume manufacturing environments

- Experience with batteries, energy storage, power electronics cooling, or other high-power thermal management

- Requirements definition and FMEA-driven development

- DoE / optimization-driven design exploration

Role Description

Form Energy is hiring a Staff Manufacturing Engineer, Electrode to support our electrode processing team. Our team is responsible for partnering with vendors to design, develop and scale cutting-edge electrode manufacturing equipment for Form Energy’s Iron-Air multi-day battery.

As a Staff Manufacturing Engineer, Electrode, you will be at the forefront of scaling our novel product, to high volume manufacturing processes. Your expertise with process scaling and rapid troubleshooting will have a direct impact on the design and operations of the equipment that creates Form’s Gas Diffusion Cathode.

Your main focus area will be calendering, drying and slitting. You will work side by side with the process engineering team who will be designing experimental trials and identifying and optimizing key process inputs. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.

Role Description
Form Energy is looking to hire a skilled, entrepreneurial, and collaborative Field Services Technician to commission and service Form’s first commercial-scale battery deployments. You will be part of the project engineering and deployment team and will work closely with engineers to install, commission, test, and troubleshoot electrical, controls, networking, and mechanical systems within our fielded commercial systems. An ideal candidate will have an aptitude for solving real world practical problems while contributing to the development of a new product at the cutting edge of clean technology.

What you'll do:

- Support installation, commissioning, operations, and maintenance of Form’s battery systems

- Perform hands-on troubleshooting of electrical and mechanical systems to determine root cause and implement mitigations

- Perform software and firmware upgrades as well as networking system configuration

- Execute commissioning and test plans to characterize the performance and functionality of battery systems

- Support emergency response at project sites to minimize plant downtime

- Lead the execution of performance testing, attain data, and communicate finding and document results to improve product performance

- Maintain company tools, vehicles, equipment, and instrumentation and a safe work environment at all project sites

- Up to 90% domestic travel to client or project sites

What you'll bring:

- 7+ years of advanced technical field experience with high-powered equipment, preferably with utility-scale energy storage systems.

- Demonstrated expertise in complex systems integration, including high-voltage troubleshooting, control circuit diagnostics, and industrial communication protocols (CAN, Modbus, Ethernet) for deep-level system debugging.

- Advanced capability to interpret and execute complex electrical schematics, engineering drawings, and wiring diagrams.

- Proficiency in operating high-voltage instrumentation (power electronics, meggers, amp clamps) and interfacing with mechanical subsystems (pumps, tanks, piping, torque/termination standards).

- Uncompromising safety mindset with extensive experience in risk assessment and operating within heavy construction environments.

- Comfort with frequent and long-term wear of heavy PPE (CAT 2 or CAT 4, steel-toed boots, face shields, chemical suits, etc.)

- Ability to maintain detailed technical documentation and asset management using modern collaborative platforms (Jira, Confluence, Slack).

- Flexibility for domestic travel (up to 90%), weekend/holiday work, and on-call availability, with a valid driver’s license.

- Proven ability to manage and influence external equipment vendors, including driving technical decisions and holding vendors accountable

Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.

Role Description
The Mechanical Engineering team at Form is focused on designing the battery cell, module, and full pack system that forms the foundation of our innovative utility-scale multi-day energy storage system. We strive to deliver designs that are optimized for performance, quality, reliability, and cost for high-volume manufacturing at Form Factory.

We're hiring a hands-on Staff Mechanical Design Engineer to own the design of subsystems within our Thermal management system. This is a critical system in Form’s iron-air battery technology and it is vital to the system’s successful operation and cell temperature control. In this role, you will play a key part in the product architecture and detailed design stages, first-of-a-kind build activities, system verification, and design for cost. You can expect to build and verify analytical models of the system, lead prototyping efforts, and work closely with controls engineers to implement the system concept of operations.

If this sounds like the right position for you, apply now! This opportunity will help shape and scale our multi-day energy storage system, contributing to the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission, contributing to a sustainable future!

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Architect, design, prototype, and test the thermal management system to meet critical performance requirements

- Build and maintain thermal system analytical models that inform design architecture decisions

- Fabricate and test first-of-a-kind prototypes to validate system design choices

- Consider ways to design the product for high-volume manufacturing and reduce product cost

- Lead critical vendor engagements and collaborate with manufacturing engineers to transition system designs from prototype to high-volume production

- Collaborate with the Electrical and Controls teams to optimize actuator and sensor integration

- Mentor junior engineers and level up our mechanical engineering best practices

- Champion safety, especially in the development of new laboratory processes

What you'll bring:

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field; Bachelor's with 8+ years of industry experience in mechanical design of equipment, liquid or gas handling systems

- Understanding of first-principles fluids modeling and experience optimizing designs for manufacturing and cost-down

- Experience working in a manufacturing environment or with contract manufacturing vendors

- Demonstrated experience optimizing mechanical design, thermodynamic systems, and interdisciplinary interfaces of fluid systems

- Sense of urgency and self-driven to hit difficult schedule targets

- Direct experience in product development within an early-stage environment ramping into production

Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.

When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. - Proven experience with electrical and mechanical design and proficiency in CAD (SolidWorks, NX, etc.)

- Expertise in cost modeling, multi-physics simulations (e.g., thermal, CFD, structural), and optimizations, with the ability to navigate system-level trade-offs and integrate them into architecture studies

- Strong mechanical and electrical engineering fundamentals, GD&T, and first principles hand calculations.

- Direct experience with high-volume manufacturing, fabrication, and prototyping techniques; experience with tight-tolerance, component design for harsh environments, DFM/DFA.

- Solid understanding of power distribution, electrical circuits, protection devices

- Superb understanding of creepage and clearance analysis and standards (ie IEC, UL etc.)

- Ability to model resistive losses, run current density analysis to optimize busbar geometry and sizing to meet system performance and mass requirements

Preferred Qualifications

- Familiar with electrical standards (NEC); experience with battery and power conversion standards (UL9540, UL1741) a plus

- Leadership, the ability to mentor, and well-developed communication, collaboration, and engagement skills working with a variety of teams and stakeholders

Role Description
In this role, you will own the end-to-end industrialization journey for plastic components—from the first sketch to high-volume production and ongoing sustaining support. You will be the bridge between our Design Engineering teams and our global supply base, ensuring that every part is designed for manufacturability (DFM) and produced under rigorous quality controls. You will not just launch products; you will implement the systems that ensure our suppliers deliver on time, meet capacity, and maintain world-class quality standards

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Lead the comprehensive technical lifecycle of thermoplastic components. Provide critical up-front manufacturing feasibility feedback during design concepts, spearhead technical evaluations for supplier selection, drive multi-stage tooling qualification (ex. T0 - T2), and establish permanent on-site process controls.

- Own and track the minimum supplier deliverables per build phase. Ensure tooling, manufacturing lines, and part accuracy mature in tight lockstep with program timelines to proactively eliminate downstream line down risks.

- Collaborate deeply with Design Engineering to conduct robust 3D DFM reviews and evaluate injection molding simulation packages (e.g., Moldflow). Proactively catch and eliminate potential manufacturing failure modes such as severe knit lines, flash, sink marks, or dimensionally unstable warp before tools are kicked off.

- Champion the phased rollout of Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) with supplier teams. Establish, review, and approve robust supplier Process Flow Diagrams (PFD), Process FMEAs (PFMEA), and formal Control Plans to systematically isolate and mitigate high-severity manufacturing risks.

- Function as the technical gatekeeper for out-of-specification components. Issue and manage Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCAR), driving suppliers through rigorous root cause analysis (8D, 5-Whys) to validate permanent corrective actions.

- Audit supplier process capability metrics for defined special characteristics to ensure the process remains statistically stable over long production cycles. Approve supplier PPAP submissions to guarantee that inspection systems yield highly reliable data.

What you'll bring:

- Bachelor’s degree in Plastics, Mechanical, or Manufacturing Engineering.

- 5+ years of experience in New Product Introduction (NPI), manufacturing, or quality engineering.

- Deep Foundational knowledge of thermoplastic molding processes (injection molding, ultrasonic welding, etc.) and secondary operations like painting or assembly.

- Familiarity with quality tools such as SPC (Statistical Process Control), Root Cause Analysis (8D), and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).

- Proven capability to read and interpret complex 2D drawings using Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) principles per ASME Y14.5. Proficiency with 3D CAD platforms to interrogate geometries, analyze assembly stack-ups, and evaluate tooling clearances.

- Excellent communication and technical authority to hold international partners accountable to strict delivery schedules and quality indices while simultaneously fostering cooperative, long-term technical relationships.

Form Energy is hiring a Senior Electronics Test Engineer for the AMU (Auxiliary Management Unit) to join our BMS Test team. In this role, you will be responsible for executing design verification and validation testing at the component, board, and system level for our AMU hardware.

Physically, the AMU PCBA sits inside the AMU Panel assembly along with the HIgh Voltage DC Shunt board which is responsible for measuring efficiency of our system, UPS, and PSUs. It acts as a critical zone controller responsible for communication, network security, high-voltage/high-current sensing, power distribution, actuation, safety/fault management, and UPS management.

You will ensure that AMU electronics meet stringent functional, reliability, safety, and compliance requirements through structured test campaigns. You’ll collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, and systems engineers to validate designs that are central to the safe and reliable operation of our multi-megawatt battery systems.This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the scaling of our battery technology and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

What you'll do:

- Test Strategy & DVP: Develop comprehensive test plans, DVP&Rs, and verification protocols for the AMU PCBA and its integrated panel assembly components.

- Communication Protocol Verification: Validate safety-critical and non-safety communication interfaces including CAN-FD (to ZMUs), Ethernet (to ZMUs and upstream QMU), and dedicated RS485 (for UPS management).

- Sensing Subsystem Validation: Design and execute test setups to verify precision sensing capabilities: Pack HV voltage (-1 to 1600V via HVDC Shunt resistor divider), Pack HV current (-500A to 500A via shunt R4), 48V PSU/UPS monitoring (0-60V), 48V total current draw (0-40A), and auxiliary temperatures.

- Actuation & Power Distribution: Verify HV contactor control (pack connect/disconnect), heater SSR control, and power routing from dual 48V PSUs and the 48V UPS down to the ZMUs.

- Safety & Fault Management: Rigorously test Hardware Over-Current Protection, fault loop logic, and Functional Safety (FuSa) testing.

- Data Analysis & Root-Cause: Analyze test data, generate detailed reports, and collaborate with design engineers to root-cause board or firmware anomalies found during testing.

- Test Automation: Contribute to test automation frameworks (utilizing Pytest) to optimize repeatability and scale verification throughput.

What you'll bring:

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

- 4+ years of experience in PCBA hardware testing. Must have robust board-level and system-level validation experience.

- 2+ years of experience in firmware verification, utilizing Pytest or similar unit testing frameworks. Comfort with debugging tools, Linux environments, and Test-Driven Development (TDD)

- Hands-on experience with test instrumentation (oscilloscopes, power supplies, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers).

- Hands-on experience with high-voltage/high-current test instrumentation (power supplies, electronic loads)

- Demonstrated ability to manage test plans, execute verification activities, and communicate findings effectively.

- Domain Knowledge: Understanding of communication protocols (CAN-FD, Ethernet, RS485), power distribution topologies, and functional safety frameworks.

The Software Systems Assurance team at Form Energy is growing! We coordinate the software architecture, requirements, and verification strategy for Multi-Day Energy Storage products that enable gigawatt-scale battery power plants.
We are looking for a Staff Software Systems Engineer to act as the technical authority bridging complex software architecture, functional safety, and embedded hardware integration. Depending on your background, this role offers the opportunity to specialize in either Broad Systems Architecture (facilitating cross-team design of distributed, safety-critical systems) or Product Assurance & Formal Modeling (using MBSE/Requirements-As-Code to translate high-level security and safety specs into executable, version-controlled schemas and bare-metal execution).

What You'll Do:

- Systems Decomposition: Distill, organize, and document the architectural structures, state machines, and requirements of a grid-scale battery electric storage system (BESS), from grid command down to battery cell firmware.

- Cross-Functional Architecture: Facilitate the design and implementation of a distributed, fault-tolerant, safety-critical system, bridging the gap between controls, electronics, and power systems engineers.

- Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Transition system state machines, Functional Safety (FuSA) Hardware-Software Interfaces (HSI), and Interface Control Documents (ICDs) from static documents into version-controlled data schemas.

- Formal Authoring, Translation & Verification: Author/translate high-level security specifications and functional safety hazard models (UL 1998/5500, ISO 21434) into verifiable execution contracts and deterministic rules.

- Disambiguation: Get in the code to get answers. You will locate and resolve ambiguity across the system, showing up for the team when context or clarity is needed.

What You'll Bring:

- 8+ years of relevant experience in software engineering, embedded systems engineering, or product assurance, including 2+ years of technical leadership experience.

- Demonstrated track record of delivering complex, production-grade embedded systems, safety-critical hardware/software, or service-oriented architectures at scale.

- Fluency in architectural design, failure/risk analysis, and cross-functional communication (diagramming, explaining, and specifying on a near-real-time basis).

- Strong foundation in discrete logic, mathematical modeling, or formal specification, with a demonstrated ability to implement executable specifications using structured data schemas (e.g., JSON Schema, Protobuf, YAML, CUE) rather than static documents.

- Ability to collaborate across diverse, interdisciplinary stakeholders to achieve unified, highly robust hardware/software designs under tight deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications:

- For the Assurance/Lab Track: Hands-on experience reading bare-metal C code and performing deep diagnostic debugging using protocol analyzers (Wireshark) and embedded debuggers across CAN, SPI, Ethernet, or Embedded Linux/MPUs.

- For the Formal Modeling Track: Direct capability to decompose complex programmable component safety requirements (e.g., UL 1998, UL 5500) into concrete software safety assertions. Experience with formal specification tools (like TLA+) is a major plus.

We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.

Role Description
The Structures Engineering team at Form is responsible for designing the structure, enclosure, and sealing systems that supports and integrates all parts of our innovative utility-scale multi-day energy storage system. We strive to deliver designs that are optimized for performance, quality, reliability, and cost for high-volume manufacturing at Form Factory.

We're seeking a Sr Mechanical Design Engineer to join our team and contribute to the scaling of our multi-day energy storage system. You'll bring components and assemblies from concept to into mass production, with an emphasis on FEA-driven structural design, weatherproofing, and manufacturability of metal enclosures. You will work cross-functionally with designers and test engineers, interrogating the potential design space and selecting appropriate test methods to validate designs. As a problem solver, you will apply your design knowledge of sheet metal, weldments, and sealing systems to balance structural optimization with design for manufacturability, weight reduction, and cost-down.

This is an exciting opportunity to be part of scaling our multi-day energy storage system at Form and contributing to a sustainable future. If this sounds like the perfect opportunity for you, apply now!

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Create white-page designs that will be the foundation of Form Energy’s next generation battery pack for high volume production

- Perform structural analysis of your designs, utilizing Ansys FEA and hand calcs

- Work closely with test team to initiate test campaigns to establish material libraries for FEA

- Collaborate with test engineers and CAE experts to validate designs through test and FEA correlation

- Present designs, analysis, and test results to broader team and leadership in design reviews

- Perform failure root cause analysis on systems and assemblies

- Travel up to 20% to other Form Energy offices or vendor sites

What you'll bring:

- Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field and 4+ years industry experience in mechanical design and structural analysis

- Experience designing complex mechanical structures, using FEA for structural analysis

- Proficiency in computer-aided design (CAD), specifically SolidWorks modeling and drafting using GD&T (ASME Y14.5)

- Experience in component design for mass manufacturing and assembly (DFMA), especially sheet metal, stampings, and weldments

- Sense of urgency and self-driven to hit difficult schedule targets

Role Description
Form Energy is scaling on every axis at once — research, first-of-a-kind manufacturing, field deployment, and the business that runs behind them — and everywhere it scales, the same pattern repeats: brilliant people held back by fragile spreadsheets, manual handoffs, and software that doesn't exist yet. As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer , you are the person we send at those problems. You will embed directly with the teams that do Form Energy's hardest work — scientists, engineers, operators, and business leaders — find the highest-leverage problems in their world, and build the software and AI that solves them. One quarter that might be a governed system of record replacing a load-bearing spreadsheet; the next, an AI agent that removes a week of manual toil; the next, a full-stack application that becomes the way a team works. You will not wait for perfect requirements or hand off to someone else to build. You go where the leverage is, ship, and stay with what you built as it matters more. This is a hands-on, senior individual-contributor role for someone who wants their work measured in problems solved, not tickets closed.

This is a hybrid role, which will require working onsite from our office in Somerville, MA or Weirton, WV 3+ days per week.

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Embed with the teams you serve — across R&D, manufacturing, field and commercial operations, and the functions that support them — to understand their hardest problems firsthand, then design and build the software that solves them.

- Hunt for leverage and act on it. Diagnose where a team is bottlenecked by missing software, manual process, or brittle tooling; make the call on what's worth building; and deliver it. Exercising judgment about what to build is as much of this job as building it well.

- Spearhead the adoption of AI-driven automation in the functions you're embedded with — prototype and ship AI-enabled tools and agents, and drive real adoption with the people who will use them, all within the guardrails set by Form Energy's independent AI-governance function.

- Own applications end to end: full-stack web applications (e.g., React / Next.js / TypeScript front ends, Python / FastAPI back ends, PostgreSQL) that become governed systems of record and decision-support tools — from data model through UI to production deployment and the users who depend on them.

- Turn expert knowledge into durable software — take the spreadsheets, notebooks, and tribal knowledge that a team runs on and turn them into correct, maintainable, owner-attributed systems that the organization can trust and build on.

- Build governed, traceable data models: versioned, append-only revision history with role-based access, so the assumptions and records that drive decisions are defensible and reconstructable.

- Integrate with Form Energy's enterprise systems — the Snowflake data platform (read-only reference data), enterprise applications (Oracle, Arena, Jama, and others), and shop-floor / operational systems — respecting each system's authoritative boundary and never writing into systems you don't own.

- Ship to production reliably: containerized services, CI/CD, and deployment on Form Energy's internal Kubernetes platform, with the observability, testing, and documentation needed to operate what you build.

- Use AI aggressively as a force multiplier in how you build — AI-assisted and agentic development — to deliver more, faster, and at higher quality than a conventional engineering approach would allow.

- Work in a fast, prototype-to-product style: get a working thing in front of users quickly, iterate beside them, and harden it into software the team can rely on — without accumulating unmanageable debt.

What you'll bring:

- 8+ years building and shipping production software, with a track record of owning complex applications end to end.

- Strong full-stack engineering skills: a modern web framework (React / Next.js / TypeScript or similar) and a production back-end language and framework ( Python / FastAPI strongly preferred ), with solid relational data modeling (PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy or equivalent).

- AI as a force multiplier — required, not optional. A demonstrated command of AI-assisted and agentic development to build faster and better, and a track record of embedding AI / ML into applications and workflows to remove toil and create leverage. You should be energized by driving AI adoption in others, not only using it yourself.

- Range and self-direction. A history of walking into unfamiliar domains, getting fluent fast, and shipping — comfortable being the sole or primary engineer on a system and owning the outcome, not just the code.

- Ability to model a complex real-world domain in software — translating messy, expert-held knowledge into correct, maintainable systems — and the rigor to enforce invariants in the data layer, not only in application code.

- Comfort working directly with non-engineering domain experts, embedded in their environment , translating ambiguous problems into shipped software — and the judgment to push back on the wrong thing and find the right one.

- Solid engineering fundamentals: version control (Git), automated testing, CI/CD, and containerized deployment (Docker; Kubernetes a plus).

- A pragmatic, ownership-minded bias toward shipping value quickly, paired with the taste to know when something needs to be built to last.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience as a forward-deployed, solutions, or embedded engineer — working alongside the users of what you build rather than behind a backlog.

- Experience building agentic or AI-automation systems for real operational workflows, and a point of view on where AI does and does not belong.

- Experience with operations research / optimization or simulation (linear / mixed-integer programming, discrete-event simulation) — a strong plus for the harder modeling problems you'll meet.

- Experience with enterprise data platforms ( Snowflake, dbt ) and the discipline of read-only vs. writable system boundaries.

- Experience integrating with ERP (Oracle), PLM (Arena), MES, or requirements-management (Jama) systems.

- Experience with enterprise identity / SSO (Microsoft Entra ID, OIDC).

- Fluency in a technical domain adjacent to Form Energy's work — hardware, manufacturing, energy, scientific computing, or laboratory/industrial environments.

- Experience in a high-growth technology or first-of-a-kind manufacturing environment.

- Partner with electrochemical, mechanical, power electronics, and controls engineering teams to orchestrate comprehensive testing, validation, and system integration strategies.

- Establish and maintain an inventory and risk register of all AI applications, skills, plugins, and agents in use, tracking ownership, data scope, and review status — including inactive or abandoned deployments.

- Define and enforce guardrails for agentic tools specifically — reviewing what actions an agent is authorized to take autonomously (e.g., sending communications, modifying records, executing code) and setting approval thresholds, logging, and rollback procedures.

- Monitor usage, cost, and performance of deployed AI tools, and manage the ongoing vendor relationship including contract renewals, model/version updates, and deprecation planning.

- Partner with IT security, legal, and business stakeholders to develop and maintain AI usage policy, acceptable-use guidelines, and an approval workflow that scales with demand without becoming a bottleneck.

- Investigate and respond to AI-related incidents (e.g., data leakage through a connected tool, unexpected agent behavior, plugin compromise), coordinating remediation and post-incident review.

- Build lightweight documentation, training, and office-hours support to help employees use approved AI tools effectively and safely, and to route new requests through the review pipeline.

- Stay current on the fast-changing AI application, plugin, and agent landscape, and proactively flag emerging capabilities or risks relevant to Form Energy.

What you'll bring:

- Direct experience evaluating, deploying, or managing AI applications, copilots, or LLM-based tools in a business or enterprise IT setting.

- Working knowledge of AI/LLM security concepts — data exfiltration risk, prompt injection, model access controls, plugin/tool permission scopes, and agent autonomy risk.

- Comfort with SaaS security fundamentals: OAuth and API permission review, third-party integration risk assessment, and access governance.

- Strong stakeholder management skills: able to run an intake/review process that business teams actually use, and to say no to risky requests without becoming a blocker.

Role Description
Form Energy is hiring a supervisor to lead our R&D Subscale Build Team. This team is responsible for creating scaled-down batteries from our electrode process teams and delivering consistent production centered around the latest advancements of our internal testing efforts. The team works on scaling, stabilizing, and continuously improving processes to fulfill our internal demand. You will contribute to the creation and evolution of lean manufacturing processes and work closely with technicians to improve quality and reliability. As the supervisor you work cross-functionally in partnership with our R&D, materials, and process engineering teams. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Team Leadership and Development: Provide coaching, training, and performance feedback to support and develop a team of 5+ technicians, Manage resourcing schedules and meet the ever changing demand from our internal customers

- Production Oversight: Lead the shift production team to ensure all production targets are met efficiently and that team follows all required protocols and standards

- Collaboration with Cross-Functional Teams: Work closely with engineering, test execution and other operational teams to troubleshoot production challenges, ensure quality and throughput are maintained at a high standard

- Be a champion of safety for a growing team and novel processes

- Aid in the introduction, scale-up, and continuous improvement of flexible internal R&D processes

What you'll bring:

- 5+ years of experience working in an R&D assembly or manufacturing environment

- 2+ years with people manager responsibilities

- Flexibility and experience in leading teams through operational changes, advocating for continuous improvement, and ensuring all team members are aligned with new work instructions and processes

- Capable of managing team resources, supporting cross-functional requests, and facilitating career development and training for team members

Role Description
Form Energy is hiring a Staff Data Engineer to build the data systems behind our deployed energy storage projects, turning real-time field telemetry into reliable, trustworthy data the rest of the company can build on. As a hands-on senior individual contributor and technical lead, you'll build and operate our operational-telemetry data products and independently lead the design of novel data solutions, raising the bar for data reliability and engineering practice by example. Your focus starts with commercial project operational telemetry and is likely to extend into manufacturing and R&D data over time, working within our data engineering group and partnering closely with field operations, hardware and controls engineers, and the analysts and application teams who depend on your data. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

- Design, build, and operate the streaming and batch pipelines that turn real-time telemetry from deployed energy-storage systems into reliable, well-modeled, query-ready datasets, spanning ingestion, transformation, storage in open table formats, and serving to downstream consumers.

- Take a lead role across the operational-telemetry data products, building on and extending the core streaming platform rather than reinventing it.

- Independently lead the design of novel data solutions, producing technical design docs and RFCs and driving them to alignment across the data, applications, and field-facing stakeholders they touch.

- Model and serve time-series and event data for downstream analytics, monitoring, and applications, using open table formats (Iceberg / Delta Lake) and time-series stores.

- Build and maintain data orchestration (Dagster, Prefect, or Airflow) for workflows that are reliable, observable, and testable.

- Stand up and manage the AWS infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi and/or Terraform) your pipelines run on.

- Partner with field operations, hardware/controls engineers, and analytics/application consumers to translate operational needs into trustworthy, well-documented data.

- Share in an on-call rotation to keep ops-critical data flowing.

- Raise the engineering bar through code review, mentorship, and technical influence that reaches beyond the immediate team.

What you'll bring:

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, software engineering, data engineering or computer engineering plus 7+ years of data or software engineering experience, including building and operating production data pipelines where reliability is operationally critical.

- Strong production programming in Python, Scala, Java, or Go.

- Hands-on experience with data transformation tools such as Apache Spark (PySpark and/or Scala) and dbt.

- Experience with open table formats such as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake.

- Experience with streaming data systems, including Kafka and/or Kinesis.

- Experience with orchestration frameworks such as Dagster, Prefect, or Airflow.

- AWS experience, plus infrastructure-as-code with Pulumi and/or Terraform.

- A track record of independently leading the design of novel solutions, including preparing technical design docs and/or RFCs.

- Excellent communication and organizational skills, and comfort participating in an on-call rotation.

- Nice to have: Databricks and/or Snowflake; industrial IoT experience and edge protocols (MQTT, Modbus, OPC-UA); time-series databases (InfluxDB, TimescaleDB, ClickHouse, Druid); REST APIs and webhooks; energy, hardware, or other physical-systems domain background.

Reporting to the Sustaining Controls Engineering Associate Manager, you will serve as the primary engineering escalation point for our Sustaining Automation Technicians. - Systems Integration & Troubleshooting: Troubleshoot and optimize MES data transactions within PLC programs, ensuring accurate product tracking and data handshakes.

- Mentorship: Provide technical guidance, training, and mentorship to Automation Technicians on the factory floor.

- On-Call Rotation: Participate in rotating on-call responsibilities for off-hour escalations from the Automation Technicians at the factory.

- Vendor & Project Management: Work directly with equipment vendors and internal teams on equipment retrofits, upgrades, and resolving long-term technical debt.

- Safety & Compliance: Ensure all plant automated equipment functions safely and correctly, strictly following Safety and Environmental policies.

- Experience: 6+ years of hands-on experience as an engineer working on industrial control systems in a manufacturing environment.

- Communication: Strong technical communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to translate complex engineering issues for operations teams.

- PLC Programming and Troubleshooting
